https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: How Our Trousers Have Shaped The Past Century (And Vice Versa)
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: The world has changed a lot in the last 100 years. In fact, it took less than 70 years to go from the first powered flight to landing on the Moon. We put wheels on suitcases. We’ve had nine different (live action) Batman films. If you asked an economist to explain this last century, they might look at a graph of real GDP. An engineer could consider the development of semiconductors. What if instead we looked at the evolution of trousers?

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/t.title: Why Is Carhartt Hollywood’s Go-To Workwear Brand?
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/t.teaser: “Putting your lead in Carhartt gives the audience something recognisable,” says Adam Cheung, style writer at British GQ. “It tells you this isn’t some superhero or billionaire genius. It’s just a normal dude trying to get through an extraordinary situation.” Cinema has a habit of slinging normal dudes into extraordinary situations. See Ryan Gosling’s science teacher turned astronaut in Project Hail Mary. Or take The Dog Stars, Ridley Scott’s upcoming post-apocalyptic sci-fi film, set in the aftermath of a – wait for it – flu pandemic that has wiped out most of humanity. Only the normal dude in this scenario happens to be Jacob Elordi.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The New Mr P. Collection Will Take You Places
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: John Deakin was what you might call an unreliable narrator. Frequently inebriated and by all accounts a bad drunk to boot, he was sacked by Vogue magazine on two separate occasions after company equipment went missing. Yet, despite being intermittently barred from many of Soho’s drinking dens, Deakin found himself at the centre of the London district’s burgeoning social scene. And, throughout the 1950s, the photographer documented the misadventures of a hedonistic clique that included the artists Francis Bacon, Lucian Freud, Frank Auerbach and Eduardo Paolozzi.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.title: 13 Lifestyle Tips To Take From The Italians
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.teaser: When it comes to the art of living beautifully, no nation has mastered it quite so well as the Italians. In the bel paese, revelling in life’s simple pleasures – be it a leisurely evening stroll with friends or beautifully cut blazer – is part of the national identity. This wonderful lust for life is something that we at MR PORTER are keen to embrace during these languorous summer months (and beyond). And as it turns out, there’s no need to hop over to the Amalfi Coast to do so (although, you can). Here, a few of our favourite Italians – and expats – have shared their secrets to bringing a touch of the dolce vita to the everyday.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Five New-To-Us Brands You Should Know About
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: These days, everyone is a curator. That’s as true of our tightly managed Instagram feeds as it is of the contentsof our wardrobes. At MR PORTER, we’re no different. Which is why we like to keep a careful eye on the brands that we stock. Everything you see here on our virtual shelves has earnt its place. And while we’re a lot nicer about it than the bouncers at Berghain, we’re still pretty rigorous when it comes to our editing process. If your name’s not down, you’re not coming in.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Stop Chasing The Perfect Fit
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: A recent episode of Architectural Digest’s Open Door series featuring Emilie and Jeff Goldblum’s Los Angeles guesthouse begins the same way as every other instalment. The couple answer the door, dressed in comfortable but stylish clothes, and beckon the camera crew inside, so they can take them on a tour. But almost three minutes into the video, Jeff saunters over to the coffee table in his piano room, picks up an oversized decorative cherry sculpture and marvels at it. “I’ve never seen this big cherry before,” he says admiringly. “I love it; we might buy that.”

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: 11 Items For Everything Autumn Will Throw At You
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: September gets a bum rap. We tend to see it as the beginning of the end: the last chance to wear that silly shirt you bought in May, or a closing window of outdoor opportunity. The truth, however, is that September is the greatest month for menswear. Its arrival heralds autumn, which in turn brings the best clothes and styling opportunities. Proper menswear is back. As F Scott Fitzgerald once wrote, “life starts all over again when it gets crisp in the fall”. Be ready for it with our guide to the new season’s essentials.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Farmer Who Broke The Internet
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: The family farm sits in the Khomas Hochland, a couple of hours’ drive from Windhoek, the capital of Namibia, along roads that feel more like tracks. If you look carefully, you’ll spot a giraffe or two casually munching on nearby trees, baboons scuttling into the bush, or oryx and springbok antelope leaping across the road in front of the car. By the time you arrive at Ruben Lambrechts’s home, you are properly in the bush: desert scrub in every direction and wildlife that treats the place less as a farm than as a shared address: a family of warthogs play in the background, a clutch of meerkats sunbathe nonchalantly nearby, a desert squirrel runs over to see who’s arrived and a young rescue zebra trails us as we explore the farm. Lambrechts, a 27-year-old cattle farmer turned entrepreneur and social-media star, is the closest thing I have encountered to a real-life Doctor Dolittle.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: What To Wear To The US Open
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: It’s fair to say that summer 2026 has been dominated by sports. And between the Knicks’ championship run and a dramatic World Cup final, New York has been at the centre of the action. The spotlight returns to the city with the US Open, arguably the last great sporting hurrah of the summer before football – of both the “soccer” and American varieties – takes over our lives once more. The question, of course, is what to wear. With record temperatures and multiple heatwaves, it’s hard to know how to dress right for it all right now. Even the most reliable summer staples can feel inadequate; getting dressed for a day at Flushing Meadows requires a little more consideration than simply reaching for a polo and calling it a day.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Introducing Fortela
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Referential design is nothing new. It is a standard practice among brands today, used to create garments that balance nostalgic appeal with a sense of contemporary freshness. Too often, however, the reference is merely performative – a superficial exercise in aesthetic nostalgia that falls short of capturing what made the original garments so compelling in the first place. With Fortela, the Milanese brand founded by Alessandro Squarzi – one of the most photographed figures in modern menswear street style – referencing the past is far more fundamental.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.title: 15 Ways To Give Your Home A Facelift
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.teaser: A man’s home, famously, is his castle. Figuratively, at least. A place you retreat to every night, a respite from the outside world. So, there’s every reason to put the time, money and effort into creating a space that works for your needs – and in which you (and anyone who happens to pass through) can really enjoy luxuriating. We asked the experts for their top tips for elevating a space, whether it’s a sprawling countryside estate or a minimal one-bed apartment in the city. Think of your entrance space as a room in itself. “Add colour and texture – a dark entrance can be incredibly dramatic,” says the New York-based interior designer Robert Passal.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Cult New Activewear Brand Worth Running Into
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Mark Bechara had been running for more than 15 years before he thought of building a business around it. He studied literature, spent years teaching and writing, and most of his career in apparel – all disparate elements that eventually converged in Literary Sport, the sportswear label he founded with Deirdre Matthews in 2022. The connection between his interests never felt forced. His running cadence had always suggested a kind of poetic narrative to him. “It was just a run, but it often felt like more than just a run,” Bechara says.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Canali’s New Exclusive Collection Takes You To Italy’s Wine Region
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: There is a particular time of the day in the northern Italian region of Piedmont, when the Langhe hills turn the colour of the prized wine they produce. As the sun drops, the upper vineyards sit above the nebbia (fog) mist, which turns the leafy slopes into shades of ruby and brick red. It’s this landscape that Canali has taken as the starting point for its new exclusive capsule with MR PORTER, Le Langhe’s Leisure Time. The Italian label has spent more than 90 years refining a singular idea of Italian tailoring that’s soft-shouldered and lightly constructed.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Standout Shades Of The Season
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Some outfits are all about the proportions. Some, the fabrics – or contrast thereof. Others, the discreet labels you find on the inside, or the loud logos on the outside. Just occasionally – and this is the part that requires a tad more thought – the outfit is the colour. Not what you’re wearing, but which shade it is. Here, five colours that will be doing all the talking this autumn – and how you can get them right.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.title: 14 Ways To Prep Your Autumn Reset
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.teaser: There is a fundamental flaw in how we approach the calendar year. In January – a month of relentless rain, sub-zero mornings and a post-holiday financial hangover – we embark upon radical self-reinvention. It’s not only unrealistic (the sunlight deficiency!), it’s borderline masochistic.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Why It’s Time To Carry A Briefcase Again
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: There aren’t many accessories out there that have fallen from grace quite like the briefcase. Forty years ago, it was the thing every single ambitious man carried. It wasn’t just somewhere to keep all your paperwork, it was a symbol of professionalism, success and, perhaps more than anything else, adulthood. If you carried one, people assumed you had important places to go and important people to see.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: How To Wear A Trench Coat Right Now
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: There are a few essential building blocks of a classic dresser’s wardrobe that a man can count on daily, in pretty much any weather. Say, a great selection of shirts, a roster of crew-neck tees, well-cut trousers, timeless jeans, hard-wearing leather shoes and a rotation of sneakers. But what about outerwear? Choosing the right coat or jacket to complete your look and to protect you from unpredictable weather requires a little more thought and investment. Take the trench coat. Humble at first glance but dig a little deeper and this storied piece now comes in every shape, colour and cut imaginable. So, where to begin?

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Why Menswear Keeps Falling Back In Love With Visvim
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Over the past few weeks, visvim has found itself on some very famous guys. Robert Pattinson has been wearing it. Timothée Chalamet, too. And, inevitably, a new group of menswearheads are googling the brand, seeing the prices and wondering what exactly they’re missing. For anyone who has been into the Japanese label for a while, though, the idea that it’s suddenly “back” doesn’t really compute. “There’s no rediscovering with them,” says Ste Wing, a Manchester-based creative director and longtime visvim fan. “If you know them and appreciate them, then you know.”

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Why You Really Need To Read More
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: There’s a very good chance that you aren’t reading this. Or, in fact, very much at all. “Numerous studies show that reading is in free-fall,” the journalist James Marriott wrote on Substack last year. “Even the most pessimistic 20th-century critics of the screen-age would have struggled to predict the scale of the present crisis. In America, reading for pleasure has fallen by 40 per cent in the last 20 years. In the UK, more than a third of adults say they have given up reading.”

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.title: Three Summer Cocktail Recipes From Our Favourite Bars
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.teaser: Summer entertaining doesn’t ask for much. Nobody expects a five-course meal when it’s 28ºC outside. What most do expect, though, is something fun, iced and in their hand within about one minute of arriving. Get that part right and you’re in the clear for whatever comes next – be it bites in the garden or something more ambitious. With that in mind, we asked three of our favourite bars for the drinks they’d make if they were the ones hosting. The results are bright, refreshing and built for repetition.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: How To Get Your Layers Right
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: To paraphrase an iconic menswear savant (Shrek), good style is like an onion – it should be layered. Building outfits from the ground up with a mix of colours, textures and shapes gives you depth and versatility, turning every look into a Russian doll of handsome menswear. It also happens to be seasonally appropriate for autumn and winter. Just as the weather changes its mind every hour, a well-layered outfit allows you to peel back a jacket or a cardigan to unveil a new look that’s as practical and considered as the one before. Need some inspiration? The five-point cheat sheet below will guide you through taking your style – quite literally – to the next level.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: A Field Guide To The Field Jacket
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: The full metal jacket of wasn’t a jacket at all, it was a bullet. Specifically, one with a hard shell and a soft core. But if it was a jacket, that jacket would be the MIL-C-43199, the hot weather “jungle jacket” worn under a flak jacket by Private Joker throughout the second half of the film – and by the director Stanley Kubrick during its filming (not in Vietnam, but east London). A similar style is worn by Al Pacino in Serpico and Robert De Niro in Taxi Driver, offering styling pointers for a civilian setting. By the latter end of the 20th century, surplus military gear made this iconic piece standard issue for countercultural rebels. But it’s also the perfect outerwear for right now.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Think You Know Your COMME DES GARÇONS?
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: The keen eyes among you will have noted the return of COMME DES GARÇONS to MR PORTER. First launched in 1969 by the pioneering Japanese designer Rei Kawakubo, the brand – French for “like the boys” – added a menswear line nine years later. More than half a century on, it’s still pushing style forward. “COMME DES GARÇONS is one of the most important brands in history,” says the Japan-based journalist Ashley Ogawa Clarke. “Every fashion nerd knows that no living designer has changed how we think about clothes more than Rei Kawakubo.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: Eddie Huang Has A Lot On His Plate
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: For at least a decade, Eddie Huang thought of himself as a writer. But when he moved to Los Angeles and started writing every day, he realised the arrangement didn’t suit him at all. “My life actually does not work when it revolves around the writing,” he says. “And the writing is actually best when it is secondary to life-living.” Life-living, too, was never going to be straightforward. Huang trained as a lawyer before walking away from a corporate firm to open his own restaurant.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: How To Get Ahead Of The Retro Sportswear Trend
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Want to get hold of a designer tracksuit this season? Then you might also have to get your skates on. “Everyone is going a little crazy for the SAINT LAURENT track jacket and I completely understand why,” says Rachel O-Williams, Personal Shopper at MR PORTER. She is, of course, referencing the viral sensation, worn by the likes of Tom Holland. “It’s the perfect meeting point between sporty and luxurious.” This intersection is important. SAINT LAURENT’s creative director, Anthony Vaccarello, has homed in on “the tension between sportswear and more sophisticated dressing,” says Benedict Browne, MR PORTER’s Style Director.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.title: 15 Ways To Be A Better Morning Person
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.teaser: Morning people wake from their sleep with ungrudging ease. They’re at their most productive when the sun has barely got out of the starting blocks. It’s because their brains are most alert and their body clocks perfectly primed for being creative and industrious. And there’s plenty of scientific evidence to show that having a positive wake-up routine comes with a whole load of physical and mental health benefits.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.title: 52 Style And Life Lessons For Men Of The World
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/l.teaser: If you’re reading this, then you’re undoubtedly a man – or a woman – of the world. Which is to say that you’ve got some experience, practical knowledge and even a touch of sophistication in the bank. You’ve been around the block, seen things and this ain’t your first rodeo. However, the smartest men – or women – also know that they know nothing, to paraphrase a long-dead Greek philosopher. And herein lies the point.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: The Exclusive Visvim Motorsport Collection Is Under Starter’s Orders
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: God forbid a man has a hobby. For some of us, an enthusiastic interest in the output of visvim is our vice – and we’re very much here that. For Hiroki Nakamura, the founder of the cult Japanese label, his calling, aside from clothes, is vintage cars. “I just love how they are designed, how they are made and how you feel when you drive [them],” he tells MR PORTER. “Driving vintage cars, racing and motorsports… It’s my passion. That’s what I do.”

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: How To Wear A Henley T-Shirt
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: Almost all of the menswear you love started out as a functional uniform for some occupation outside the fashion industry. Trench coats, blouson jackets, cargo pants and desert boots, for example, can all be traced back to the military. And those Carhartt double-knees you live in would never have been on your radar were they not endorsed by the world’s blue-collar workmen decades ago. The sports industry has had a big hand in shaping modern menswear, too. And few athletic garments have had such staying power as the classic Henley.

https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.title: How To Wear A Leather Jacket (Without The Midlife Crisis)
https://www.mrporter.com/en-gb/journal/f.teaser: The words “leather jacket” can too often prompt a wince in fashionable circles. It’s an item indelibly associated with the male midlife crisis – the kind of look that might attempt to channel Bruce Springsteen in the 1970s but ends up more like a long-lost Top Gear presenter. Too-tight, outmoded outerwear worn in a vain attempt to signal he’s “still got it”.
